# vaultwarden_organization_api_key (Ephemeral Resource)

Reads the API key of an organization, for the Bitwarden public API and Directory Connector, without storing it in the plan or state. Requires Terraform 1.10 or later.

The organization gets an API key the first time it is read. Reading it requires the provider user's master password and, on Vaultwarden 1.37 and later, the `Owner` role in the organization (1.36 also allows `Admin`). To rotate the key, use `vaultwarden_organization_api_key_rotation`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vaultwarden_organization" "example" {
  name = "Example Organization"
}

ephemeral "vaultwarden_organization_api_key" "example" {
  organization_id = vaultwarden_organization.example.id
}

# Pass the key to a write-only attribute, for example to store it in AWS Secrets Manager
# for the Directory Connector, without saving it in the state
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "example" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.example.id
  secret_string_wo = jsonencode({
    client_id     = ephemeral.vaultwarden_organization_api_key.example.client_id
    client_secret = ephemeral.vaultwarden_organization_api_key.example.client_secret
  })
  secret_string_wo_version = 1
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) Client ID of the API key, `organization.<organization_id>`.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of the API key.
- `revision_date` (String) When the API key was created or last rotated.
